In this section of *HEA Anthology Web*, the teaching focuses on direct observation of the mind: *"It becomes revealed to the hero along the way that this is an illusion and the mentor, whose name is Morpheus, presents the hero Neo with a choice: the blue pill or the red pill."* The central guidance is to step back from the habitual impulse to control or fix present experience, and instead cultivate a spacious, non-reactive presence. When we investigate thoughts and feelings without identification (*anattā*), their grip on the heart naturally dissolves. It is like It is like a small boat floating on a calm mountain lake beneath an open sky. Rest in that clear, unentangled knowing.

The text reflects: *"If you HAPPILY EVER AFTER take the blue pill, it means your mind will continue to be absorbed in the delusion."* Thoughts are merely passing mental formations (*saṅkhāra*); they have no solid core unless we feed them with belief. When a thought arises, simply recognize it as 'thinking, thinking' without jumping into the storyline. It is like It is like a deep ocean holding waves on its surface while remaining utterly still below. Be the vast, open sky through which thoughts pass like harmless clouds.
